Film review

Wildwood (2026)

Reviewed by Caz
18 November 2026

5/5

Caroline’s rating

Read the review ↓
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:01
Instaread

Prue a teenager who had been struggling with her life sets out on a mission into a forest outside Portland after her young brother was kidnapped, the world beyond the trees was like nothing she could have imagined.

Wildwood is a truly magical journey into a totally different world, with a unique stop motion animation style which is visually stunning.

The story sees Prue attempting to find her baby brother Mac who had been taken by crows, she’s not alone though as Curtis is with her. Even though she had tried to get rid of him earlier, as she actually thought he was a little bit geeky and not her type of person.

From the moment they can get into the forest, even though they had no idea that a little bit of magic was involved everything they thought they knew about the world was about to be turned upside down. Talking animals, crazy stories and the splits in the different types of animals and people resulting in hostility and potental wars.

Everything about each scene just looked breathtaking and I felt fully enthralled in the world I was seeing unfold, the story had many twists and turns. I feel like I feel to mention the animation style as it really did feel great, and even though you knew it was animated it actually felt quite real at times – which I am hoping makes sense.

The themes embedded throughout were hard hitting, just thinking back to the opening scene and how tragic that was to see unfold. Then the pressures of growing up and being concerned with how people see you. Which I think is why Curtis was such an amazing character, he was rather timed and that bit geeky and everything he went through in the forest really demonstrated why you shouldn’t make instant judgments.

This is easily one of the best films of the year.

It is currently the longest stop-motion-animated film of all time, at 2 hours and 12 minutes.
